data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is strictly more resilient to correlated design flaws because it naturally maintains design independence, whereas the large service's strictly greater component redundancy is illusory if all components share the same flawed specification.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The large service intentionally employs N independent design teams with diverse specifications.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized network operators all use the same open-source library, negating design independence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The correlated failure is caused by a shared environmental factor rather than a design flaw.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A large service with N redundant components may have zero design redundancy if all components are built from the same specification. A latent flaw in the specification (e.g., a misunderstanding of a cryptographic protocol) renders all N components simultaneously vulnerable. A decentralized network, composed of independently designed services, will naturally exhibit design diversity because different teams solve the same problem differently. This design diversity acts as a true redundancy against correlated specification flaws, making the decentralized network more resilient to this class of correlated failure despite having fewer redundant components.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
